topics.label: Introduction to complement
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system and frames its conceptual significance and nomenclature challenges within immunology.

topics.label: Overview and core principles of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational logic, naming conventions, and central role of component C3 in driving complement activity.

topics.label: Mechanisms of complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the three distinct recognition cascades initiate complement activation and reach a local trigger threshold on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector processes through which activated complement directly eliminates pathogens and recruits immune responses.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host tissue protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins prevent inappropriate complement activation and protect host cells from destruction.

topics.label: Clinical pathology of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct clinical presentations and disease risks associated with specific genetic and acquired complement deficiencies.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens utilize diverse evolutionary strategies and molecular mechanisms to evade complement-mediated killing.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the discussion on complement and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
